questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: What it's like to be a twin and why twins fascinate us
How doctors can tell if twins are identical
Famous Hollywood stars who have twins
Why twins are becoming less common
questions.why: They discuss our fascination with twins and the good and bad sides of being one.

questions.q: What question would Neil ask a twin?
options: Have you ever swapped boyfriends?
Do you feel each other's pain?
Can you read each other's minds?
Do you have the same dreams?
questions.why: Neil says he might ask, 'Do you share each other's thoughts?'

questions.q: According to presenter Anand Jagatia, how might twins react to these common questions?
options: They might be happy to explain
They might show they're bored or annoyed
They might refuse to talk to you
They might ask you exactly the same questions in return
questions.why: He says don't be surprised if they roll their eyes at you.

questions.q: What does Professor Karen Dillon say is good about being a twin as a child?
options: Twins usually get better marks at school because they study together
Parents give twins more attention
Twins never argue with each other
Going through school and making friends together is easier
questions.why: She says you go through school and make friends together, so childhood milestones are easier.

questions.q: What problem does Karen Dillon describe as twins get older?
options: People see them as a twin rather than as an individual
They start to look less similar
They usually have to live far away from each other for work or study
They find it hard to make any friends
questions.why: She says people really think of you as a twin rather than as an individual.

questions.q: Why are twins useful to scientists?
options: They live longer than other people
They can share their thoughts with each other during scientific experiments
They share genes, so their differences show the role of environment
They are born with psychic powers
questions.why: Because twins are so genetically similar, differences between them tell scientists a lot about nature and nurture.

questions.q: Why does Anand mention twins who were separated at birth?
options: To show that adoption is usually a bad idea
To explain why twins have the same dreams
To prove that the environment matters much more than the genes we have
To wonder how much control we have over our lives
questions.why: He says their similar lives make you think, 'How much choice have I had over the way my life's turned out?'

questions.q: Which of these was NOT true of the 'Jim Twins'?
options: They both married a woman called Linda
They grew up together in the same town
They both gave their dog the same name
They met each other again when they were both 39 years old
questions.why: They were separated at birth and reunited at 39, so they did not grow up together.
